[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding truthfully (bid = value) is a weakly dominant strategy. It maximizes expected profit because your bid only determines whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). Underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable; overbidding risks paying above value if others bid high. With value 44 and no informative history (single round), bid 44 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 44 and pay that second-highest price. ]

[ With independent private values and a second-price (Vickrey) auction, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value.
